title: Authentication & Authorization

sections.markdown: **Authentication (AuthN)** = proving who you are. **Authorization (AuthZ)** = deciding what you're allowed to do. Different steps, in that order.
At an airport: your **passport** is authentication (you are who you claim); your **boarding pass** is authorization (you may board this flight, this class). One identity, many permissions.

## Authentication factors
- **Something you know**: password, PIN.
- **Something you have**: phone, hardware token, OTP.
- **Something you are**: fingerprint, face.
MFA combines two or more.

rows: Any server verifies with a key

sections.markdown: Hash passwords with bcrypt/argon2 (never plain or MD5/SHA1). Enforce least privilege. Always check authorization on the **server** — never trust the client.

flashcards.back: Authentication proves identity; authorization grants permissions. AuthN first, then AuthZ.
Sessions revoke instantly (delete it); JWTs are hard to revoke before expiry — use short TTLs or a blocklist.
RBAC grants by role; ABAC grants by attribute rules (more flexible, more complex).

quiz.explain: You prove identity (AuthN) before the system decides permissions (AuthZ).
